issues.kind: example contradicts law 2 (a) with law 3 (the bent group's fixed two-edge path)
issues.claim: Law 2 (a) (l. 2810–2813) gives a line an event or costless rule sets "the lawful shape law 3 picks nearest it" and a points-form `drawWall`'s trace to "its own cost choosing among" the shapes law 1 admits. Law 3's key (2) (l. 2846–2852) ranks a re-laid line by its largest distance from the old, then the area between them. The bent-group sentence nonetheless fixes the replacement's path (l. 3203–3206): "(i) an unlawful crossing by the nearest lawful one along the deck … — the line from its entry point along that side's edge to it, across the strip there and along the other edge to its exit point —". Its (iv) reuses it: "the line bent through it by (i)'s path" (l. 3215–3216). Every bent-group member is a stroke, a drag, a costless rule's line or a points-form `drawWall` (l. 3178–3182). Worked case: a hand stroke meets an aqueduct's deck line at a standing support where the channel runs above the wall's top, which law 1 (2) makes unlawful; its nearest lawful crossing Q lies under the next span, d along the deck. (i)'s path is a rectangle d wide over the strip's whole width. A line from the entry point to Q to the exit point, its band clear of the ring, is lawful (law 1 (4); law 1 (2), over). It has the same largest distance d and encloses less area, so law 3 ranks it first. The two builds lay different lines, and with them different wall strips over the under-deck strip and different spans read `open` (law 1 (8)). For a points-form trace, (i)–(iii) pin moves law 2 (a) leaves to its own cost. (ii) and (iii) agree with law 3 for a stroke. No bar asserts (i)'s path: T110-2 (4) asserts the crossing law 3 picks (l. 19463–19472) and (ii)/(iii) at the entry-side edge (l. 19496–19500). So a build that follows the laws passes every named test and §5.3's row. An example's slip: minor.
issues.required_change: model — the bent-group sentence (l. 3203–3204): "Every other part of the line inside the strip is replaced, between the points where the line enters and leaves the strip:" → "Every other part of the line inside the strip is replaced, between the points where the line enters and leaves the strip, by the lawful shape law 2 (a) gives it (a stroke's or a costless rule's line the one law 3 picks nearest it; a points-form `drawWall`'s trace its own cost's), these its cases:"; (i) (l. 3205–3206): "— the line from its entry point along that side's edge to it, across the strip there and along the other edge to its exit point —" → "— the line between its entry and exit points re-laid through it —"; (iv) (l. 3216): "the line bent through it by (i)'s path" → "the line re-laid through it as (i) re-lays a crossing".

issues.kind: example citation names a subset of law 2's order (form F3's residue)
issues.claim: Row W1's last column (l. 3346): "no lawful shape: (G3) — a hand op refused once its own pull, within its own search band, finds no lawful shape, its band never widened and never a stage left unwalled (law 2 (a), (c))". §5.2's F-WALL ladder cell (l. 9862) carries the same words for a hand `contractWall` or a terrain stroke's cliff re-anchor, "(§2.7's laws, law 2 (a), (c))". The hand op's pull is S5a's trace step (W1: "a hand `contractWall` (H: S5a's trace step, §4.11)"). That step resolves a barred pin by law 2 in its order, "(a) moved along its way, the trace laid through it, (b) its way re-routed, (c) …" (*beneath*, l. 3087–3089; *No gate and no tower*, l. 3150–3153). The fourth pass moved W14's identical "(law 2 (a), (c))" to "law 2, in its order" (adjudication-r7y.md M7, VF7x-EPO-02, F3) and §7.3 (b) 3's likewise (D5, VF7x-HND-02). These two sites, written for VF7v-HND-04 (adjudication-r7w.md M7, D4), kept the subset. A build reading the parenthesis as the order would refuse a hand contraction whose barred pin (b) re-routes. But the text names "its own pull", which runs (b), and §5.3's row decides nothing else: a citation, minor (the grade of VF7x-EPO-02 and VF7x-HND-02).
issues.required_change: model — row W1's last column (l. 3346): "its band never widened and never a stage left unwalled (law 2 (a), (c))" → "its band never widened and never a stage left unwalled (law 2, in its order; §4.4 S5a *Trace* (2))"; END determinism — §5.2's F-WALL row, its ladder cell (l. 9862): "its band never widened and never a stage left unwalled (§2.7's laws, law 2 (a), (c))" → "its band never widened and never a stage left unwalled (§2.7's laws, law 2, in its order; §4.4 S5a *Trace* (2))".

held_notes.note: Persists (adjudication-r7y.md's held note 11). §4.6 words the under-deck strip S8 holes as the deck's ground projection over its piers and spans; §2.7's term words it as the deck's plan between its feet. The open question is whether a ramp's or stair's plan lies in the strip. Both are holed as (6)'s reservation, so the difference shows only where a reader reads the strip alone (raised way × plots).
